turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: No, ma'am, I'm afraid I don't know where Estella is. I didn't see her when I came in, and I wouldn't know how to find her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You are expected to know the whereabouts of my adopted daughter, and you should not pretend otherwise. I warn you, Pip, to be more attentive and respectful.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm very sorry, ma'am, if I've caused any trouble, but I'm not sure I know how to find Estella, and I'm afraid I wouldn't know what to do if I did, even if I found her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will find Estella in the garden, playing with the music box she has been so fond of lately.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I'll be able to play with Estella, ma'am, I'm afraid I'm in a bit of a hurry and I have to get back home soon.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will waste no more time, Pip, and play with Estella at once. I will not be kept waiting.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I don't think I should play with Estella if she's in the garden, I'm not sure it's right for me to...

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will do as I say, Pip, and play with Estella. I will not be ignored or disobeyed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I understand, ma'am, what you mean by me playing with Estella, I don't know if I'm the right person for her to play with

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with Estella, Pip, because I have ordained it. She is waiting for you, and you will not disappoint me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But, ma'am, I don't think I'm the right sort of person for Estella to play with, my family's not very... respectable, and I'm afraid I might make things awkward for her

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You dare to question my judgment, Pip? You, a lowly boy from the marshes, dare to imply that you are not worthy of association with my own Estella?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't want to cause any trouble, ma'am, and I was hoping you might understand that I'm not very good at playing games with young ladies

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will do as I say, Pip, and play with Estella, for it is her fate to be courted and to court, and you will be the one to test her mettle.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But, ma'am, I'm afraid I don't know how to play with someone like Estella, she seems so... so refined, and I don't want to make a mistake in front of her

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you would do well to remember that Estella is a product of my own design, and it is I who shall dictate how she shall be treated and entertained. You will play with her, and you will do so with the utmost seriousness and gravity, lest you incur my displeasure.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I must decline, ma'am, for I fear I would only bring shame to myself and to your esteemed household if I were to attempt to play with Miss Estella

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you would do well to remember that I am not a 'ma'am' to be trifled with. You will play with Estella, and you will do so immediately, lest you suffer the consequences of my displeasure.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I humbly beg your pardon, Miss Havisham, but I fear I am not suited for such a task, and I would rather not bring any discomfort to yourself or Miss Estella

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You are a coward, Pip, and I will not be made a fool of by your feeble excuses. You will play with Estella, and you will do so with the proper demeanor and respect, or you will leave my house immediately.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
